- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.15) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +0.61 sentiment) by overshooting 2–5% in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 68–70), model often holds too high; adjust downward by 2–4% for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses late-period reversals (e.g., 70→65→70); add 1–2% buffer for volatility spikes near end of horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.27 or -0.16 patterns, model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% true, 30% sentiment).
